decisions.executionNote: Establish elbow-up bend and raise left wrist before approaching the mallet, whose handle is now horizontal near the center.
Move left wrist inward above the handle while gradually aligning the downward gripper across the horizontal shaft.
Continue the overhead handle approach, retaining the established elbow-up branch and open gripper.
Finish downward orientation and center the left fingers over the handle's left end; descend cautiously for visual refinement.
Refine lateral alignment from the wrist image, lower onto the shaft, and begin closing the left gripper.
Center the shaft between the fingers, close fully and lift 5 cm to verify that the mallet is retained.
Mallet appears retained. Carry it above the leftmost key, keeping the shaft pointing right so the left wrist can remain in its own workspace throughout the sequence.
Move the retained mallet farther left and forward, raising for clearance before the first red-key strike.
Tap the leftmost red key vertically, then lift by more than 2.5 cm before moving right. Contact height remains visually estimated.
Refine the first-key contact slightly right and lower; pause at the bottom to inspect tip placement before advancing.
Lift 4.5 cm from the red key, move right one key spacing, and strike the orange key while retaining the mallet.
Finish the orange-key downstroke, lift 4 cm, advance to yellow, and strike vertically with a slightly lower contact target.
Settle the yellow strike, lift 4.5 cm, advance one key to green, and lower for the next strike.
Complete green contact, lift the mallet 4.6 cm, move to the fifth light-blue key, and strike downward.
Finish the light-blue strike, lift 4.6 cm and advance to the sixth dark-blue key, keeping the left wrist on its own side.
Settle the sixth key, lift 4.5 cm, and advance to the seventh purple key for a vertical strike.
Replan after the continuity guard: complete the lift in smaller increments, then move over the seventh key and begin its downstroke.
Use small increments to lower onto the seventh key while drawing the wrist back and yawing the shaft slightly forward, preserving tip alignment and reach margin.
Settle the seventh strike, lift 3.6 cm, and approach the last key. Draw the left wrist back slightly with compensating yaw for a comfortable elbow-up reach.
Strike the eighth, rightmost key, pause briefly at contact and lift the retained mallet 4 cm clear.
Increase the final post-strike clearance and hold the mallet steady, keeping the wrist back to retain reach margin.
Completion is not confirmed. Return above the left end with the tip slightly pitched down, preparing a more definite left-to-right contact sequence.
Move fully above the red key before descending, using the slightly downward-pitched mallet to make a clear first contact.
Correct the tip from the left wooden edge onto the red bar and make a controlled deeper contact before restarting the ordered sequence.
The tip appears to have deflected at the red-key edge. Lift clear, recenter slightly right, and tap red again without pushing as deeply.
Lift 5.1 cm from red, advance to orange, and tap vertically at the visually established contact height.
Lift fully from orange, center the tip over yellow, and strike with a brief contact pause.
Lift the mallet 5.1 cm clear of yellow, advance to green and strike at the same contact height.
The shaft appears to have slipped during contact. Lift clear, recenter over green, and increase tip-down pitch to keep the handle off preceding keys.
Replan from the guard stop and descend slowly onto the center of green, maintaining the new tip-down orientation.
Lift 4 cm after green and move above the fifth key, compensating shaft yaw with wrist retreat to preserve reach margin.
Center on the fifth light-blue key and lower slowly to contact, with the gripper kept closed.
Lift clear after the fifth strike, slightly reduce downward pitch and retract the wrist, then align above the sixth key without crossing the arms.
Lower the tip onto the sixth dark-blue key in small vertical increments and pause to inspect contact.
Lift 4 cm from the sixth key and position over the seventh purple key, drawing the wrist back slightly to maintain reach margin.
Strike the seventh purple key, pause at contact, then lift the mallet 3.6 cm before advancing.
Approach the eighth key while leveling the mallet slightly to extend tip reach without moving the left wrist across the centerline.
Strike the rightmost key with a controlled downstroke, pause at contact, then lift the retained tip more than 2.5 cm.
Increase the final lift and draw the wrist safely back, then hold the retained mallet clear while observing the result.
Return clear above the left end for one continuous sequence using the now-stable grasp and fixed orientation; earlier slips leave completion uncertain.
Center over the red key and make a slow downstroke with fixed orientation, avoiding the excessive depth that previously disturbed the grasp.
The tip is left of the red bar. Lift clear, shift right onto its center, and repeat the first strike before advancing.
Lift 5.1 cm from the centered red strike, advance one key spacing, and tap orange with fixed orientation.
Lift clear of orange and strike the yellow key next, retaining the fixed grasp and orientation.
Lift 5.1 cm after yellow, advance to green, and strike with the same stable orientation and contact height.
Lift clear of green and strike the fifth light-blue key slightly farther from its end pin, maintaining the grasp orientation.
The mallet has visibly shifted in the grasp. Lift away from the keys and retreat into the left workspace to recover a stable handle grasp.
Lower the shifted mallet onto the clear table area to prepare a new grasp nearer the handle end.
Release the mallet on the table and move the open left gripper toward the handle's tail for a fresh, longer-reach grasp.
Align the handle within the wrist view, lower the fingers around its tail and close fully for a fresh grasp.
Allow the fingers to close on the shaft, then lift 7 cm and check that the mallet follows without slipping.
The mallet follows the new grasp. Move it forward and slightly upward above the first red key, keeping its diagonal shaft orientation fixed.
